source_caption:
To establish the absolutely merciless reality of their silent world, director John Krasinski made a deeply disturbing personal choice for the film’s shocking opening sequence. When the youngest son activates the noisy toy space shuttle on the bridge and is instantly snatched away, the terrifying creature that kills him was actually played by Krasinski himself. Having written, directed, and starred in the film alongside his real-life wife Emily Blunt as a way to explore the terrifying anxieties of parenthood, Krasinski insisted on donning the motion-capture suit for that specific moment. By literally becoming the very monster that slaughters his own on-screen child, Krasinski masterfully proves that the most paralyzing cinematic horror does not just come from the alien predators lurking in the dark, but from the crushing, universal terror of failing to protect the ones you love.
⠀
A Quiet Place (2018), directed by John Krasinski, starring Emily Blunt, John Krasinski, Millicent Simmonds. In a devastated, post-apocalyptic world completely overrun by blind, hyper-sensitive alien predators, a fiercely resilient family must live in absolute silence, desperately communicating only through sign language to survive the terrifying creatures that hunt by sound.

source_details.synopsis: A Quiet Place is a 2018 American post-apocalyptic horror film directed by John Krasinski. Made from a screenplay co-written by Krasinski, Scott Beck, and Bryan Woods based on a story Beck and Woods conceived, it tells the story of a mother (Emily Blunt) and father (Krasinski) who struggle to survive and raise their children (Millicent Simmonds and Noah Jupe) in a post-apocalyptic world inhabited by blind extraterrestrial creatures with an acute sense of hearing. Beck and Woods developed the concept for the story while in college and began writing the screenplay in January 2016.
